item: The governor's closed windows travel in the diagnostics zip (new collect_perf_windows member), paid for by fewer ticks
refs: R181; Q58 = b; PR #1464 (carries the rows PR #1455 added)
summary: R181 (Q58 = b) waits on a diagnostics zip from a slow-network machine that shows its real best permit count. A window record rides the one tick that closes a window (a window is read after 240 s, so at most one tick in 160), and the zip kept only the newest ticks (20 in the quick copy, 200 in the whole one), so it showed one window or none, never the staircase of permit counts and rates a pass walked. window_history() reads the log's closed windows (all 5,000 rows it holds) into one compact row each (ts, pass_id, permits, permits_next, articles_stored, closing_tick_kbps, which is the closing tick's rate and not the window mean collector_kbps, and the window's own fields) and returns {windows, held, kept, partial, reason, skipped_rows}: a missing or unreadable log is windows null with the reason, never an empty list; a damaged row (not JSON, not an object, undecodable bytes) costs only itself and is counted. The zip gets it as a new collect_perf_windows member: the newest 11 in the quick copy, the newest 31 in the whole one, with held/partial saying when the log held more (a slow machine's log can hold more than 31). The budget is uncompressed debug-bundle.json bytes, pinned by test against the widest row built from the governor's own record (400 B) and the least a tick row measures when CollectionMonitor._tick runs with no vitals (about 1,600 B, measured in the test, not typed): the quick copy keeps 17 ticks instead of 20 and the whole one 192 instead of 200. Deflated, the quick copy is about 700 B larger of about 2 KB (an independent read measured it): net zero is claimed before compression only. Row sizes are from this tree's writers; the 18 Oct lab logs and the Lenovo bundle gave the first figures. The budget still needs an independent re-measure on a real written log (the Export lane, which owns collect_perf).
